requirement: Fetch a list of URLs concurrently with aiohttp while never exceeding a concurrency limit, returning one result per URL in input order and recording connection failures instead of aborting the batch.
skeleton: A frozen FetchResult dataclass and fetch_all validating the limit, sharing one semaphore across per-URL coroutines that catch aiohttp.ClientError, and gathering them in order.
caption: Bounded concurrent fetching with aiohttp and asyncio. FetchResult is a frozen dataclass of url, status, body and error. fetch_all(session, urls, *, limit=5) raises ValueError saying limit must be at least 1, creates one asyncio.Semaphore(limit) shared by every task, and runs one coroutine per URL through asyncio.gather, which returns results in input order rather than completion order. Each task holds the semaphore around session.get and returns the status and resp.read() body, so non-2xx statuses such as 404 are data, not errors; an aiohttp.ClientError becomes a FetchResult with no status or body and the exception class name, so one dead host never cancels the batch. The fixture asserts, with a TestServer counting requests in flight, that 12 URLs at limit 3 peak at exactly 3 and keep their bodies in order, that the default peaks at 5, that a slow URL listed before a fast one stays first, that a refused port yields error ClientConnectorError beside a 200 and a 404, and that limit 0 raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Crawl many endpoints quickly without overloading them
constraints: At most limit requests are in flight, default 5
One semaphore is shared by all tasks
aiohttp.ClientError becomes a result with the error class name instead of propagating
HTTP error statuses are reported as statuses

rationale.teaches: Share one asyncio.Semaphore across tasks, catch per-task client errors, and use gather to keep results aligned with inputs.
rationale.why: A semaphore per task limits nothing, as_completed scrambles the pairing of inputs and outputs, and an uncaught error in one task fails the whole batch.

ops.docstring: Fetch many URLs concurrently with aiohttp under a concurrency limit.

ops.source:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FetchResult:
    """Outcome of one fetch: a status and body, or the error class name."""

    url: str
    status: int | None
    body: bytes | None
    error: str | None

candidates.why_wrong: Each task creates its own semaphore, so nothing limits concurrency.
The semaphore allows one fewer request than the limit.
A single connection failure raises out of gather and loses every other result.
The default allows 10 concurrent requests instead of 5.
Results come back in completion order, so they no longer line up with the input URLs.
